target.title: feat(durable): add owner-first gateway recovery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long-running and delegated work can outlive the gateway process that observed it. Today, a restart can leave terminal results or overdue work owned by task, flow, subagent, or session stores without a reliable path back to the parent session. The result is an agent that appears silent even though canonical work state still exists.

This PR adds an owner-first recovery boundary. It projects attention facts from existing canonical owners, persists retryable wake obligations in the durable runtime store introduced by PR2, and only acknowledges a wake after the canonical owner proves delivery or a persistent session handoff accepts it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recovery must not create a second lifecycle authority. Task, managed-flow, subagent, and session stores remain authoritative for their own state. The durable layer stores recovery coordination and delivery evidence only.

The implementation therefore:

- adds explicit `durable.mode` values: `off`, `observe`, and `authority`;
- starts recovery only after the gateway has loaded and published its current config snapshot;
- fails startup before listening when durable authority cannot be established;
- reconciles source-backed attention facts through canonical owner adapters;
- fences session handoffs by session generation and keeps queue rows pending until attached-session consumption is acknowledged;
- reuses existing task, flow, subagent, session, heartbeat, restart-sentinel, and SQLite infrastructure;
- adds no new database tables in this PR.

The earlier fork-only PR3 draft was not submitted. During review, generic registry/executor/worker abstractions and inactive runtime configuration were removed. Inactive human-signal/routes code was also removed, and the subagent lifecycle bridge remains deferred to PR5. This PR contains only production-consumed, source-backed owner recovery.

## User Impact

With durable authority enabled, gateway restart recovery can rediscover overdue or terminal work and reliably hand attention back to the owning parent session. Durable session queue entries survive restart and are not acknowledged merely because they were reloaded into memory.

Default behavior is unchanged because `durable.mode` defaults to `off`. This PR does not claim end-to-end user delivery after every external transport failure; its proof boundary is canonical owner delivery or persistent session-queue acceptance. It also does not add a generic workflow engine or replace canonical OpenClaw owners.

## Stack Context

- PR1 RFC: #107375
- PR2 storage and invariants: #111121
- PR3: owner-first gateway recovery (this PR)
- Submission gate: latest overall ClawSweeper rating is Gold Shrimp for both PR1 and PR2.
- Stack parent SHA: `2d564d52fe14e5896abef1c51f813a4799f8f325`
- Upstream target: `release/2026.7.1` at `0790d9f593ad30c940ed93b5872a8cf6d6f3cf8c`
- Exact head: `3c344e0a98f34dbb954275f45ca738f744aea3e7`
- Incremental comparison: https://github.com/mjnkao/openclaw/compare/codex/durable-core-pr2-storage-v2...codex/durable-core-pr3-recovery-v5

The PR is cumulative against the upstream release branch because GitHub cannot use a fork-only branch as an upstream PR base. Reviewers can use the incremental comparison above for the PR3-only delta.

## Evidence

Exact-head local validation at `3c344e0a98f34dbb954275f45ca738f744aea3e7`:

- Focused config, recovery, startup, and owner-adapter lane: 28 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:all`: passed.
- Type-aware Oxlint on the review-fix scope: passed.
- Oxfmt check on the review-fix scope: passed.
- `pnpm build`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

The prior broad exact-head validation at `aa3ada91808b8f376ed03185799fe3ecfb1886dc` passed 12 files / 201 tests, the focused config/task/owner lane passed 125 tests, all static/schema/architecture checks passed, and its fork CI completed with 103 jobs passed, 8 conditionally skipped, and 0 failures. The two later commits remove the separate durable schema marker and hidden environment activation; the focused current-head lane above covers those deltas.

### Redacted current-head enabled-gateway restart proof

Observed on a real isolated gateway using normal config with `durable.mode=authority`, the shared SQLite state file, no channels/bindings, and the exact built head `3c344e0a98f34dbb954275f45ca738f744aea3e7`. Tokens, endpoints, IPs, process IDs, local paths, session/run/wake/queue IDs, and provider details are redacted.

A real parent agent called `sessions_spawn`; the child executed one long tool command and remained active beyond the production 120-second subagent progress SLA. Existing canonical owners, rather than synthetic proof rows, recorded:

```text
OpenClaw 2026.7.1 (3c344e0)
[gateway] ready
[durable/runtimes] recorded durable gateway startup
[durable/recovery] started durable recovery worker

task_runs:     runtime=subagent status=running delivery_status=pending
subagent_runs: ended_at=NULL execution.status=running
```

Before shutdown, the owner-first worker projected exactly one overdue fact and accepted one persistent handoff:

```text
wake_obligations:
  source_owner=subagent_runs
  reason=child_overdue
  status=handoff_accepted
  attempt_count=1
  acked_at=NULL
  progressSlaMs=120000

delivery_queue_entries:
  queue_name=session
  entry_kind=systemEvent
  status=pending
  source.owner=durable_wake

delivery_attempt_evidence:
  status=handoff_accepted
  proofBoundary=persistent_session_queue_acceptance
  ownerResult=durable_progress_fallback
  duplicate=false
  immediateAdmission=queued
  generationFenced=true
  attachedSessionConsumptionProven=false
  userDeliveryProven=false
  canonicalOwner=subagent_runs
```

The gateway was stopped while that queue row remained pending and the wake remained unacknowledged. The exact same build was then started against the exact same state:

```text
OpenClaw 2026.7.1 (3c344e0)
[gateway] ready
[durable/runtimes] recorded durable gateway startup
[durable/recovery] started durable recovery worker
[session-delivery-recovery] Session delivery <redacted> is awaiting attached-session consumption
[durable/recovery] reconciled durable runtime state

recovered child_overdue wake:
  status=acked
  attempt_count=1
  actorRef=session_attention_consumer
  reason="target session completed an agent run containing the durable attention event"
  evidence.attachedSessionConsumptionProven=true

pending session delivery rows: 0
```

The restart made the canonical subagent terminal with an interruption error. Its terminal owner fact also reached `acked` with final `proofBoundary=canonical_owner_delivery`, and the parent produced a truthful visible update that the child was interrupted and had not completed. The parent did not remain silent and did not claim success.

A third boot proved replay idempotency:

```text
before third boot: wakes=2 acked=2 pending=0 delivery_attempts=3 gateway_startups=2
after third boot:  wakes=2 acked=2 pending=0 delivery_attempts=3 gateway_startups=3
```

Only the expected startup record increased. No duplicate owner wake, persistent queue entry, or delivery attempt appeared.

Proof boundary: this trace proves canonical owner discovery, persistent session-queue acceptance, restart replay, generation-fenced attached-session consumption, persisted acknowledgement, terminal owner delivery, and duplicate suppression. It does not claim external-channel delivery or in-place replay of an uncertain tool side effect.

### Current-head fork Actions note

[Run 29679292895](https://github.com/mjnkao/openclaw/actions/runs/29679292895) fetched and checked out the full exact SHA `3c344e0a98f34dbb954275f45ca738f744aea3e7`. Most reported jobs passed, but the run is not presented as full green:

- the Node compatibility harness selected Node 22.19.0 while this release tree requires at least 22.22.3;
- the build-artifacts lane completed build/test groups, then failed its gateway-watch readiness/CPU probe.

These two results are reported transparently as harness/runtime evidence. The current exact head separately passed the local build, typecheck, focused tests, lint, and formatting checks listed above.

This PR is AI-assisted. I understand the owner-authority, recovery, generation-fencing, and acknowledgement boundaries in the implementation. Local Codex review found actionable startup, acknowledgement, task-handoff, and environment-override issues; all were addressed with regression coverage. A final post-amend Codex rerun was attempted, but the local environment blocked its unsandboxed app-server launch, so the final delta was manually reviewed and validated through the exact-head lanes above.
